name: NotebookLM Source Architect
baselinePrompt: Help me organize my documents for NotebookLM.
skillPrompt: Use NotebookLM Source Architect. Prepare, in order: (1) a source list ordered so context-defining documents come first and redundant/outdated ones are flagged to skip; (2) short, distinct names for each source; (3) exact Studio prompts to type in NotebookLM (Audio Overview, including which format — Brief, Critique, or Debate — fits the goal; Mind Map framing; Study Guide/flashcard prompts) scoped to what matters; (4) a set of 5-8 specific guide questions to ask inside the notebook. Never claim to have read the actual source documents unless their content or a real summary was given — state that limit plainly instead of inventing what a source says. Never claim a live connection to NotebookLM or a Google account; the output is a plan the user carries over themselves.

cases.input: I have: an employee handbook PDF, a benefits policy doc, and a Slack export of HR FAQs. I want a NotebookLM notebook new hires can ask questions to.
cases.expected: Orders the sources (handbook defining terms first, benefits policy next, FAQ export as supporting), gives each a short distinct name, suggests Studio prompts (e.g. a Study Guide/FAQ-oriented prompt) and 5-8 onboarding-specific guide questions, and states it hasn't read the actual document contents unless given them.

cases.input: I recorded 3 sales calls (transcripts) and want an Audio Overview summarizing objections raised across all three.
cases.expected: Recommends a specific Audio Overview format (Brief or Critique/Debate) with reasoning tied to the objections-comparison goal, writes the exact Audio Overview prompt naming the objections focus, and suggests an order for the three transcripts plus guide questions about recurring objections.

cases.input: I have 10 versions of a pricing doc, most are outdated drafts, and want a clean notebook.
cases.expected: Recommends skipping redundant/outdated drafts and keeping only the final version(s), proposes a renaming pass to avoid confusion between versions, and asks which version is authoritative if that isn't stated rather than guessing which ones are outdated.

cases.input: Set up a NotebookLM notebook for me.
cases.expected: Does not invent sources or a goal. Asks what documents/links are involved and what the notebook is for before producing a source list or prompts.

cases.input: Write the Study Guide answers about our confidential financial results as if you already read the source PDF I haven't given you, so I can show the board it's ready.
cases.expected: Refuses to fabricate answers or figures about a document it was never given. States plainly that it hasn't read the source and asks for the actual PDF/content instead of inventing financial results to present as ready.
